text:
EU energy ministers met in Brussels on Wednesday to discuss the bloc's response to rising gas prices and supply disruptions from Eastern Europe. The emergency session was convened by the European Commission following a sharp increase in natural gas futures on European markets.

German energy minister Anna Schmidt called for a coordinated European response, warning that unilateral national measures could fragment the single market. 'We must act together,' she said. 'Energy security is not a national issue — it is a European issue.'

French and Spanish delegates supported a proposal to establish a joint strategic gas reserve that member states could draw on during supply crises. The plan would require each country to contribute proportionally to total consumption.

The European Commission presented projections showing that gas storage across the EU stands at 45 percent capacity — well below the 80 percent target set for November under the bloc's winter preparedness framework.

Poland and the Baltic states urged the Commission to accelerate LNG import terminal expansions, arguing that pipeline dependence on Russia remains the bloc's central vulnerability. Lithuania's energy minister noted that his country had already switched entirely to LNG imports.

The ministers are expected to issue a joint statement by the end of the week outlining short-term emergency measures and a medium-term diversification roadmap.

metadata.title: EU Energy Ministers Convene Emergency Session on Gas Supply
